The constant-displacement input e = (0,0,1,0) has norm 1; the output of T_{R_n}Psi_n(s)e is (0,q_n/sqrt(M_a),0,0). With the E velocity-inner-product weight Lambda^{-1} used in P:cameron-spatial-map, the dual w_n = (0,Lambda q_n/||q||_{H^{1/2}},0,0) has norm 1 and gives <T_{R_n}Psi_n(s)e,w_n>_F = ||q_n||_2^2/(sqrt(M_a)||q||_{H^{1/2}}) =: c_a > 0, independent of J and R_n because translation preserves ||q||_{H^{1/2}}. Thus every finite C fails, identical to the prior calculation; adding 'On [0,1]' only makes explicit the interval already implicit in the ODE solution and norm, and no conclusion is changed.
